title: The WPA band directors, Gilbert and Martina
summary: Gilbert classified the musicians by ability and built the band up; Martina replaced him and put out those who could not play.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I'm the one who got Lewis the man in the WPA band. In fact, I was the first trumpet player in the WPA band, could play anything that people could understand. There was a bunch of them in there. But Gilbert had the band then. Gilbert had the band way before Martina came. And what Gilbert did, he got in there and he'd taken everybody who said he was a musician. Then he classified him. He classified him just like a school, like it started from first grade on up. And he rated him according to their plan abilities.
I don't know if the last name was Gilbert. I can't think of it.
Nothing. He was just a director of the WPA band.

Yeah. Well he classified the men which he would benefit the musicians more than anybody they had there if they'd let him see it there. But they felt like he wasn't doing it the way they wanted and they got rid of Gilbert and they got old man Martina. And that broke up all his ideas was. His ideas was to get so many men together that couldn't play that much and let somebody go over and teach them and rate them on like that. And the men that was qualified could read pretty good, you know, it would be a band up with them. Which it was a better building ability for musicians than it was when Martina came. When Martina took it over, instead of him building it up he tore it up. See because everybody couldn't play he put them out of the band.
So he didn't give him a chance to learn.
He didn't give him a chance to learn. That broke it down you see. That's a shame. Back to Garnier. Who was in Garnier's band usually?
